comments.value: I see flawed (LLM generated) reasoning that this would improve performance, when in reality requiring to load the full body mesh and a default outfit would be less performant than having those avatars optimized and uploaded separately with one outfit per avatar.

@{68098a4626271974ef4d2775|full_name}, yes i used Copilot to help write that since i am not very good at writing. question what is more demanding on your network and virtual memory? downloading an entire avatar about 150mb and then downloading another avatar about 148mb because that egirl decided to change from an avatar with a skirt to one with a swimsuit, or just download the avatar one time, and when she wants to change into a swimsuit, you only download that 2mb swimsuit and drop from memory the skirt? This is how most MMOs handle clothing since it is a waste of resources to have a full model built for every possible outfit combination.

details:
Summary

This proposal suggests a modular outfit streaming system for VRChat avatars. Instead of forcing every client to download an avatar’s entire wardrobe, creators would upload a base avatar plus separate outfit modules. The client downloads only the selected outfit, and unused outfits are unloaded from memory. The base avatar can also specify a default outfit so users never load into worlds undressed unless they choose to.

Problem

Avatars often include many full outfits and accessories. Because VRChat packages everything into one file:

• 	Clients must download all outfits even if only one is used.

• 	VRAM and RAM usage increase due to unused textures and meshes.

• 	Performance ratings are inflated by inactive toggles and hidden geometry.

• 	Avatar files can reach 150 to 300 MB, causing long load times.

• 	Quest and future mobile platforms struggle with memory limits.

• 	Creators must build complex FX controllers and toggles.

This creates unnecessary strain on users, creators, and VRChat’s servers.

Solution

Introduce a modular system where an avatar consists of:

• 	A base avatar

• 	One or more outfit modules

• 	Metadata linking modules to outfit selections

• 	A default outfit module that loads automatically

When a user selects an outfit, the client downloads the required modules and unloads the previous ones. Performance rating updates based on the active modules only.

How It Works

Creator Workflow

Creators upload:

• 	The base avatar

• 	Outfit modules such as clothing, accessories, hairstyles

• 	Metadata defining outfit flags, dependencies, performance estimates, and the default outfit

VRChat packages these into a modular avatar bundle.

Client Behavior

When an avatar loads:

• 	The base avatar downloads first.

• 	The default outfit module downloads immediately unless the user has chosen a different outfit.

• 	When switching outfits, the client downloads the new modules and unloads the old ones.

• 	Performance rating recalculates based on active modules.

Networking

Only the outfit flag is synced. Other clients automatically fetch the correct modules.

Performance Rating

Rating is based on active meshes, materials, textures, PhysBones, and animator complexity. Inactive modules do not count.

Benefits

Smaller Downloads

A base avatar might be 20 to 40 MB. Each outfit might be 5 to 15 MB. Clients download only what they need.

Lower Memory Usage

Unused outfits no longer occupy VRAM, RAM, or CPU time. This reduces crashes and improves stability.

Accurate Performance Ratings

Ratings reflect the outfit actually in use.

Better User Experience

• 	Faster avatar loading

• 	Smoother outfit switching

• 	Less lag in crowded worlds

• 	Better support for Quest and future mobile devices

Reduced Server Load

Smaller downloads reduce bandwidth and CDN costs.

Simpler Creator Workflow

Creators no longer need dozens of toggles or large FX controllers. Outfits become modular assets.

Technical Notes

Rig Compatibility

Modules reference the base armature and are merged at runtime.

Module Limits

VRChat can enforce limits such as:

• 	Maximum module count

• 	Maximum module size

• 	Maximum total avatar size

Caching

Clients may cache recently used modules to avoid repeated downloads.

Backward Compatibility

Existing avatars continue to work normally. Modular streaming is optional.

Conclusion

Modular outfit streaming would significantly improve performance, reduce memory usage, and shorten download times. It gives creators cleaner workflows, reduces server load, and prepares VRChat for future platforms. Allowing a default outfit ensures users always load in fully dressed unless they choose otherwise. This system solves long-standing issues with avatar size, complexity, and performance while keeping VRChat flexible and creator-friendly.
title: Modular Outfit Streaming for VRChat Avatars
